Roundworms
triplets.tail: Eggs shed in feces, embryonate in environment in 2–4 weeks to infective L3 stage

triplets.head: Roundworms
triplets.tail: Eggs survive in soil for years

triplets.head: Roundworms
triplets.tail: Young animals undergo hepato-tracheal migration (intestine → liver → lungs → coughed up/swallowed → intestine)

triplets.head: Roundworms
triplets.tail: Older animals: somatic larvae become arrested/dormant in tissues (liver, lungs, brain, muscles)

triplets.head: Roundworms
triplets.tail: Ingestion of embryonated eggs from contaminated environment

triplets.head: Roundworms
triplets.tail: Yes — visceral/ocular larval migrans in humans

triplets.head: Hookworms
triplets.tail: Eggs hatch in 2–9 days, develop to infective L3 in soil

triplets.head: Hookworms
triplets.tail: Migration: bloodstream → lungs → coughed up/swallowed → small intestine

triplets.head: Hookworms
triplets.tail: A. caninum somatic larvae arrest in tissues, reactivate during pregnancy for transmammary transmission to puppies

triplets.head: Hookworms
triplets.tail: Adults attach to intestinal wall, inject anticoagulants, feed on blood; live 4–24 months

triplets.head: Hookworms
triplets.tail: Yes — cutaneous larval migrans in humans

triplets.head: Whipworms
triplets.tail: Lemon-shaped eggs with polar plugs; larvate in ~10 days in warm humid conditions; infective stage is L1 inside egg

triplets.head: Whipworms
triplets.tail: Eggs extremely resistant — survive years in soil; require high humidity

triplets.head: Whipworms
triplets.tail: Ingested eggs hatch in small intestine → mucosal migration + 4 molts → adults in caecum/large intestine

triplets.head: Whipworms
triplets.tail: Adults live >1 year; embed anterior end into mucosa

triplets.head: Whipworms
triplets.tail: Fecal-oral only: ingestion of embryonated eggs

triplets.head: Dipylidium caninum
triplets.tail: Proglottids (rice-grain segments) shed in feces → egg packets consumed by flea larvae → cysticercoid develops inside flea → pet ingests infected adult flea during grooming

triplets.head: Dipylidium caninum
triplets.tail: Can also rarely be transmitted via dog biting louse (Trichodectes canis)

triplets.head: Taenia spp.
triplets.tail: Eggs in feces → consumed by intermediate hosts (rodents, rabbits, livestock) → cysticerci develop in tissues → pet eats infected prey

triplets.head: Echinococcus spp.
triplets.tail: Tiny adults (5–6 mm) in dog intestine → eggs in feces → consumed by intermediate hosts (sheep, rodents, humans) → hydatid cysts in organs → dogs eat infected organs

triplets.head: Echinococcus spp.
triplets.tail: Includes E. granulosus (sheep strains) and E. multilocularis (rodent strains)

triplets.head: Dipylidium caninum
triplets.tail: Ingestion of infected flea during grooming

triplets.head: Taenia spp.
triplets.tail: Ingestion of prey animals containing cysticerci

triplets.head: Echinococcus spp.
triplets.tail: Ingestion of organs from infected intermediate hosts

triplets.head: Echinococcus spp.
triplets.tail: Highly zoonotic — hydatid cyst disease in humans

triplets.head: Ollanulus tricuspis
triplets.tail: Transmission via ingestion of vomitus containing L3/L4/adults; worms survive in vomit up to 12 days

triplets.head: Ollanulus tricuspis
triplets.tail: Ingestion of vomitus from infected cat

triplets.head: Physaloptera spp.
triplets.tail: Larvated eggs consumed by insect intermediate hosts (cockroaches, crickets, beetles) → L3 develop → pet eats infected insect or paratenic host (frogs, lizards, mice)

triplets.head: Physaloptera spp.
triplets.tail: Ingestion of insect intermediate hosts or paratenic hosts (frogs, lizards, mice)

triplets.head: Ollanulus tricuspis
triplets.tail: No reliable OTC treatment — requires veterinary diagnosis and prescription

triplets.head: Coccidia
triplets.tail: Cystoisospora canis, C. ohioensis, C. neorivolta, C. burrowsi

triplets.head: Coccidia
triplets.tail: Unsporulated oocysts shed in feces → sporulate in environment (requires 65–100°F, as fast as 6–16 hours)

triplets.head: Coccidia
triplets.tail: Ingestion → sporozoites invade enterocytes → schizogony (asexual multiplication) → gametogony (sexual stage) → new oocysts

triplets.head: Coccidia
triplets.tail: Oocysts survive up to 1 year in environment

triplets.head: Coccidia
triplets.tail: Paratenic hosts (mice, rats) can harbor zoites in tissues

triplets.head: Coccidia
triplets.tail: Fecal-oral: ingestion of sporulated oocysts from contaminated environment

triplets.head: Coccidia
triplets.tail: No OTC treatment available — prescription required

triplets.head: Giardia
triplets.tail: Cyst stage: thick-walled, immediately infective when shed; resistant to chlorination and freezing

triplets.head: Giardia
triplets.tail: Trophozoite stage: pear-shaped, flagellated; attaches to enterocytes in proximal small intestine via ventral adhesive disc → causes malabsorption/diarrhea

triplets.head: Giardia
triplets.tail: Encystation occurs as trophozoites move down intestine → new cysts shed in feces

triplets.head: Giardia
triplets.tail: Partially treatable — Fenbendazole is OTC but off-label dosing requires vet supervision; Metronidazole is prescription-only

triplets.head: Giardia
triplets.tail: Fenbendazole (50 mg/kg for 3–5 days, requires vet guidance)

triplets.head: Toxoplasma gondii
triplets.tail: Dogs, humans, and other mammals (intermediate/dead-end hosts)

triplets.head: Toxoplasma
triplets.tail: Complex — cats are the only definitive host

triplets.head: Toxoplasma
triplets.tail: Three infective stages: sporozoites (in oocysts), tachyzoites (acute, rapid multiplication), bradyzoites (chronic, tissue cysts in brain/muscle)

triplets.head: Toxoplasma
triplets.tail: In cats: ingestion of tissue cysts or oocysts → intestinal epithelium invasion → 5 types of schizonts → gametogenesis → oocysts shed in feces for 1–3 weeks

triplets.head: Toxoplasma
triplets.tail: Oocysts sporulate in environment in 1–5 days (2 sporocysts × 4 sporozoites each)

triplets.head: Toxoplasma
triplets.tail: In intermediate hosts: sporozoites/bradyzoites convert to tachyzoites → spread via macrophages → immune response → convert to bradyzoites in tissue cysts → persist for life

triplets.head: Toxoplasma
triplets.tail: Dogs do not shed oocysts; are dead-end intermediate hosts

triplets.head: Toxoplasma
triplets.tail: Ingestion of sporulated oocysts from cat feces

triplets.head: Toxoplasma
triplets.tail: Major zoonotic risk — toxoplasmosis, especially dangerous for pregnant women

triplets.head: Toxoplasma
triplets.tail: No OTC treatment available — prescription required

triplets.head: Heartworm
triplets.tail: Indirect — mosquito is obligate intermediate host/vector

triplets.head: Heartworm
triplets.tail: L1 microfilariae circulate in host blood → mosquito ingests during blood meal → L1→L3 development in mosquito over 10–20 days

triplets.head: Heartworm
triplets.tail: L3 deposited in skin via mosquito bite → L3→L4 in 7–14 days → L4 migrates through tissues → L4→L5 in 45–60 days → enters pulmonary arteries → matures to adult in ~6 months total

triplets.head: Heartworm
triplets.tail: Adults: 15–36 cm (6–14 inches); live 5–7 years in dogs, 2–3 years in cats

triplets.head: Heartworm
triplets.tail: In cats: most larvae killed by immune response; dying larvae cause HARD (Heartworm-Associated Respiratory Disease)

triplets.head: Heartworm
triplets.tail: Mosquito bite only (>30 species can serve as vectors)

triplets.head: Heartworm
triplets.tail: No OTC treatment or prevention available — all heartworm preventatives require prescription

triplets.head: Aelurostrongylus abstrusus
triplets.tail: Adults in alveolar ducts/terminal bronchioles (~9–10 mm); eggs hatch in lungs → L1 coughed up, swallowed, passed in feces

triplets.head: Aelurostrongylus abstrusus
triplets.tail: L1 consumed by slug/snail → develop to L3 → paratenic hosts (rodents, frogs, lizards, birds) can harbor L3 → cat ingests infected gastropod or paratenic host

triplets.head: Angiostrongylus vasorum
triplets.tail: Adults in pulmonary arteries and right ventricle; L1 in feces → consumed by slugs/snails → develop to L3 in ~17 days → dog ingests gastropod or frog paratenic host

triplets.head: Angiostrongylus vasorum
triplets.tail: L3 penetrate gut wall → develop in abdominal lymph nodes → enter portal circulation → migrate to pulmonary arteries/right heart; can cause coagulopathies

triplets.head: Lungworms
triplets.tail: Ingestion of slug/snail intermediate hosts or paratenic hosts (frogs, rodents, lizards, birds)

triplets.head: Lungworms
triplets.tail: Partially treatable — Fenbendazole is OTC but requires longer courses (10–14 days) under vet supervision for lungworms

triplets.head: Fleas
triplets.tail: Ctenocephalides felis (most common, affects both dogs and cats)

triplets.head: Fleas
triplets.tail: Complete metamorphosis, 4 stages, mostly off host

triplets.head: Fleas
triplets.tail: Eggs: pearly white, 0.5 mm; laid on host, fall off within hours; female lays 40–50/day starting 20–24 hrs after first blood meal

triplets.head: Fleas
triplets.tail: Larvae: maggot-like, ~0.5 cm; feed on organic debris + flea feces (blood); avoid light; develop in carpets, shaded soil, under furniture

triplets.head: Fleas
triplets.tail: Pupae: cocoons (~0.5 cm); can remain dormant up to 30 weeks; emerge when stimulated by heat, CO₂, vibration

triplets.head: Fleas
triplets.tail: Adults: feed immediately; live 2–3 months; emerge in 14–35 days depending on climate

triplets.head: Fleas
triplets.tail: Wildlife visitors introducing fleas to environment

triplets.head: Fleas
triplets.tail: Dipylidium caninum (tapeworm), Bartonella henselae, Rickettsia typhi, R. felis, hemoplasmas, Francisella tularensis

triplets.head: Fleas
triplets.tail: K9 Advantix II (dogs ONLY — toxic to cats)

triplets.head: Ticks
triplets.tail: Most are three-host ticks (different host each stage); full cycle 1–3 years

triplets.head: Ticks
triplets.tail: Acquire pathogens in larval/nymphal stages; transmit in nymphal/adult stages

triplets.head: Ticks
triplets.tail: R. sanguineus (brown dog tick) can complete entire cycle indoors on same host

triplets.head: Ticks
triplets.tail: Pathogen transmission via saliva during feeding; Lyme disease typically requires 24–48 hrs attachment

triplets.head: Ticks
triplets.tail: Lyme disease, Ehrlichiosis, Anaplasmosis, Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever, Babesiosis

triplets.head: Ticks
triplets.tail: K9 Advantix II (dogs ONLY — toxic to cats)

triplets.head: Ear Mites
triplets.tail: Direct; entirely on host; 5 stages: egg → larva → protonymph → deutonymph → adult

triplets.head: Ear Mites
triplets.tail: Full cycle: 18–28 days; adults live ~2 months

triplets.head: Ear Mites
triplets.tail: Non-burrowing; feed on epidermal debris; primarily in ear canal but ectopic infestations possible

triplets.head: Ear Mites
triplets.tail: Cats can harbor >1,000 mites per ear

triplets.head: Ear Mites
triplets.tail: Direct close contact (highly contagious); easily transfers between dogs and cats

triplets.head: Ear Mites
triplets.tail: Treatable with OTC medications (prescription products preferred)

triplets.head: Ear Mites
triplets.tail: Pyrethrin-based ear drops (Adams Ear Mite Treatment, PetArmor)

triplets.head: Sarcoptic Mange Mites
triplets.tail: Female burrows into epidermis (tunnels ~1 cm in 4–5 days) → lays 2–3 eggs/day for up to 2 months → eggs hatch in 3–4 days

triplets.head: Sarcoptic Mange Mites
triplets.tail: 6-legged larva → molting pockets → protonymph → tritonymph → adult; full cycle ~21 days

triplets.head: Sarcoptic Mange Mites
triplets.tail: Fomite transmission — mites survive off-host for several days

triplets.head: Sarcoptic Mange Mites
triplets.tail: Zoonotic — causes temporary itchy dermatitis in humans (resolves when dog treated)

triplets.head: Sarcoptic Mange Mites
triplets.tail: Partially treatable — Frontline (fipronil, OTC) has some off-label efficacy but is not reliable as sole treatment; prescription recommended

triplets.head: Demodectic Mange Mites
triplets.tail: Direct; entirely in hair follicles and sebaceous glands

triplets.head: Demodectic Mange Mites
triplets.tail: Stages: fusiform eggs → 6-legged larva → protonymph → deutonymph → cigar-shaped adult (D. canis 180–210 µm)

triplets.head: Demodectic Mange Mites
triplets.tail: Full cycle: 20–35 days; normal skin flora; disease occurs with immune deficiency

triplets.head: Demodectic Mange Mites
triplets.tail: Dam to neonate via skin contact during nursing (primary route)

triplets.head: Demodectic Mange Mites
triplets.tail: No OTC treatment effective — prescription required

triplets.head: Lice
triplets.tail: Direct; entire life cycle on host

triplets.head: Lice
triplets.tail: Eggs (nits) cemented to hair shafts → 3 nymphal instars → adults; full cycle ~21 days; adults live ~28 days

triplets.head: Lice
triplets.tail: Biting lice feed on skin debris; sucking lice feed on blood

triplets.head: Lice
triplets.tail: Direct contact between animals of same species

triplets.head: Lice
triplets.tail: Trichodectes canis can serve as intermediate host for Dipylidium caninum (tapeworm)

triplets.head: Cheyletiella Mites
triplets.tail: Large eggs (240 µm) attached to hair by silk threads → prelarva (non-feeding legless sac) → 6-legged larva → 2 nymphal stages → adult (500 µm, visible to naked eye)

triplets.head: Cheyletiella Mites
triplets.tail: Full cycle: ~3 weeks; non-burrowing but may create pseudo-tunnels; feed on tissue fluids

triplets.head: Cheyletiella Mites
triplets.tail: Highly contagious direct contact; NOT host-specific (transfers between dogs, cats, rabbits)

triplets.head: Cheyletiella Mites
triplets.tail: Adults survive off-host for several weeks (fomite transmission)

triplets.head: Cheyletiella Mites
triplets.tail: May be transported by fleas, lice, flies

triplets.head: Cheyletiella Mites
triplets.tail: Zoonotic — causes itchy red papular rash in humans

triplets.head: Cheyletiella Mites
triplets.tail: Partially treatable — Frontline (fipronil, OTC) has off-label efficacy; prescription products more reliable

triplets.head: Fenbendazole
triplets.tail: OTC as single-dose packets; also available by prescription for specific formulations

triplets.head: Fenbendazole
triplets.tail: FDA-approved for roundworms, hookworms, whipworms, tapeworms in dogs

triplets.head: Fenbendazole
triplets.tail: Not FDA-approved for cats; used off-label

triplets.head: Praziquantel
triplets.tail: Non-prescription tablets available at pet stores; injectable and combination products are prescription-only

triplets.head: Seresto collar
triplets.tail: Over-the-counter (OTC) — #1 selling non-prescription flea & tick brand

triplets.head: Capstar
triplets.tail: Adult fleas (kills within 30 minutes, single dose)

triplets.head: K9 Advantix II
triplets.tail: Dogs ONLY — TOXIC TO CATS (permethrin is fatal to cats)

triplets.head: Pyrethrin-based ear drops
triplets.tail: Adams Ear Mite Treatment, PetArmor Ear Mite Treatment

triplets.head: CDV vaccine
triplets.tail: Inactivated (killed) — shorter DOI, not recommended as primary choice

triplets.head: CAV vaccine (CAV-2)
triplets.tail: Modified Live Virus (MLV, CAV-2 for cross-protection against CAV-1)

triplets.head: Rabies vaccine (dogs)
triplets.tail: Licensed 1-year or 3-year DOI (actual DOI may be longer)

triplets.head: Rabies vaccine (dogs)
triplets.tail: As mandated by local law (typically 1 or 3 years)

triplets.head: FPV vaccine
triplets.tail: Every 3 years or longer for low-risk cats

triplets.head: FHV-1 vaccine
triplets.tail: ≥ 3 years (Jas et al., 2015); protection is partial

triplets.head: FHV-1 vaccine
triplets.tail: Partial protection at 7.5 years with 52% efficacy (Scott & Geissinger, 1999)

triplets.head: FHV-1 vaccine
triplets.tail: Feline Viral Rhinotracheitis (FVR) / Feline Herpesvirus Infection

triplets.head: FCV vaccine
triplets.tail: ≥ 3 years (Jas et al., 2015); protection is partial

triplets.head: FCV vaccine
triplets.tail: Partial protection at 7.5 years with 63% efficacy (Scott & Geissinger, 1999)

triplets.head: Rabies vaccine (cats)
triplets.tail: Recombinant (canarypox-vectored, non-adjuvanted) — e.g., Purevax; reduces risk of feline injection-site sarcoma (FISS)

triplets.head: Rabies vaccine (cats)
triplets.tail: Licensed 1-year or 3-year DOI (Purevax recombinant validated for 3-year DOI)

triplets.head: FeLV vaccine
triplets.tail: Cats (newly designated core in 2024 WSAVA for endemic areas: kittens <1 year and adult cats with outdoor access)

triplets.head: FeLV vaccine
triplets.tail: FeLV-negative testing is mandatory before vaccination

triplets.head: Canine Distemper
triplets.tail: ~50%; survivors often have permanent neurological damage

triplets.head: Canine Distemper
triplets.tail: Muscle twitches, especially face/jaw ('chewing gum fits')

triplets.head: Canine Distemper
triplets.tail: Hyperkeratosis of nose and footpads ('hard pad disease')

triplets.head: Canine Distemper
triplets.tail: Tooth discoloration — permanent, in puppies infected before permanent teeth emerge

triplets.head: Canine Distemper
triplets.tail: Immunosuppression leading to secondary bacterial infections

triplets.head: Infectious Canine Hepatitis
triplets.tail: Jaundice/icterus (rare in acute cases, more common in chronic)

triplets.head: Infectious Canine Hepatitis
triplets.tail: 'Blue eye' — bilateral corneal opacity/edema appearing 7–10 days after recovery (~25% of recovered dogs)

triplets.head: Infectious Canine Hepatitis
triplets.tail: 'Paint brush' hemorrhages on gastric serosa, lymph nodes, thymus, pancreas, subcutaneous tissues
